issue.title: id: Phase 13 plan — client shells and capability providers
issue.body:
## Part 1 — Phase 13 design

Writes the full Phase 13 plan at `.opencode/plans/phase-13-client-shells.md` and closes **#564**.

The plan holds D1-050..D1-056 and names F12.7, F12.14 and F12.12 as stepping stones:

- **F13.1** the versioned shell contract (client↔server frame spec + conformance check) — #783
- **F13.2** SSH as a transport for the frame protocol (`id world join --via ssh`) — #784
- **F13.3** SSH-over-iroh reachability (and iroh-over-SSH fallback) — #785
- **F13.4** presentation capability tiers with in-band terminal detection — #786
- **F13.5** kitty keyboard protocol on the raw input path — #787
- **F13.6** native client shells on the shell contract — #788
- **F13.7** client-side capability providers under the ceiling model — #789
- **F13.8** multi-server, multi-client topology; client-only mode always supported — #790

Each F13.x has an exit criterion (acceptance criteria) in the Phase 11/12 style, plus scope/non-goals, architecture (client-shell variants + capability-provider model + data/sync touchpoints), security/trust, sequencing, risks and open questions. No Phase 13 code is implemented in this session — design + issues only.

## Part 2 — id issue triage

Triage of the open id issues not owned by other train sessions (skipped: #643 Session E, #539–#555 Session B, #534 + #556–#560 Session C, #564 this PR, #783–#790 this PR).

- **Fixed: 0** — no code fixed here. `pkgs/id` does not build on main (p2panda hash mismatch, #643 / Session E's fix), so any Rust change in `pkgs/id` could not be test-verified, and the small web bugs (#724/#732/#761/#770/#756/#749/#745/#331) are Phase 0–10 web-client territory under Session A's review.
- **Categorized: 46**, each with a `id train triage (2026-10-24):` comment carrying one category + one line of evidence:
  - `needs-decision`: **25** (Phase 2–6 owner-default confirmations, SSH/tracking home questions, web bugs assigned to Muse → Session A, #779 to Session E)
  - `too-big-needs-design`: **18** (Phase 2–6 sync/membership design gaps, F11.2/F11.3/F11.12/F11.11-remainder, web sync PeerHistory, E2E/CI stabilization, D1-043/044)
  - `blocked-on-*`: **2** (#168 → groups-fold/provisioning ingest wiring; #565 → #541 pinned Roc compiler)
  - `obsolete`: **1** (#538 → superseded by this Phase 13 plan / #788–#789)

End state: every open id issue is fixed by a train session, owned by one, or carries a triage category.

issue.body:
## What and why

Designs for how SSH (and other terminal) sessions take input and present worlds, beyond the raw default and `cmd:` line mode that shipped in #211. Each needs a design, or a research package where marked, before implementation. Ticked when its design is committed and an implementation issue exists. Not tracked: D1-049 (two SSH channels on one connection), which both reports say not to build until a real client exists.

## Items

Each box is done when the design (or research package) is committed and an implementation issue is linked here.

- [x] **D1-040 — Documents as a session frame pair (web/CLI parity)** (M, design)
  Move `/documents` and `/document` from an SSH-local blob read to a `documents`/`document` ClientFrame/ServerFrame pair in world_session.rs, like `records`, so web and CLI clients can read world documents too.
  - Status: not started. `grep -n '"documents"\|"document"' pkgs/id/src/world_session.rs` finds nothing; documents exist only in world_ssh.rs (:455).
  - Source: RPT §7 Step 1 'Decision to record'; RPT §16 Q3; RPT §12 Later
  - Prerequisites: #548 — D1-039 Fix #211 reconciliation gaps: total records cap, document output through `send`, per-world document store
  - Design: `doc/2026-11-01T16-05-00Z_design_documents_session_frames/` (PR #3760, merged 2026-11-01); implementation: #3762
- [ ] **D1-045 — In-session command toggle (prefix key + visible mode indicator)** (M, research package)
  While in raw mode, a prefix key (Ctrl-P or `~ Enter`) opens a command prompt line with a visible indicator; /quit or the prefix returns to raw. Only if users ask for it.
  - Status: not started. The raw arm of `SshIo::recv` forwards bytes unconditionally (pkgs/id/src/world_ssh.rs:421-424); there is no prefix handling.
  - Source: REF:106-112, 135-149 (shape 3, triggers); RPT §7 Step 3.1; RPT §16 Q4
  - Prerequisites: #546 — D1-041 One line grammar shared by SSH command mode, `id world join` pump and CLI verbs (+ `--command-mode`)
- [ ] **D1-046 — Split UI on one PTY (world grid + pinned command row, focus routing)** (L, research package)
  The server draws the world region plus a pinned bottom command row, and keystrokes route by focus; buffered output to the command region enables server-side autocomplete mid-game. The web client already has this shape (separate chat form).
  - Status: not started. No region or focus state in pkgs/id/src/world_ssh.rs; the web split exists (RPT cites pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts:524-533 chat form).
  - Source: REF:88-93 (shape 1); RPT §5 shape 1; RPT §7 Step 3.2
  - Prerequisites: #562 — D1-044 Incremental (diff) ANSI renderer instead of full clear-repaint, D1-045 In-session command toggle (prefix key + visible mode indicator) (in this list)
- [ ] **D1-048 — Roc partial-line surface: non-journaled 'viewer is typing' notification to guests** (L, design)
  Pass the viewer's partial line to the program so a Roc app can render live autocomplete or a validating form. It is a new guest-facing surface and needs its own design: which event carries it, that it is never journaled, and its bounds.
  - Status: not started. Guests receive only committed `Input` bytes and `System` events (RPT cites sandbox.rs:677-685); no typing event kind exists in `WorldEventKind`.
  - Source: REF:161-164; RPT §5 'Extended to Roc apps'; RPT §7 Step 3.4
  - Prerequisites: D1-046 Split UI on one PTY (world grid + pinned command row, focus routing) (in this list), #534 (tracking issue) — D1-025 F12.7 Versioned guest ABI spec, plaza_abi_version export, conformance suite
- [ ] **D1-052 — Presentation capability tiers with in-band terminal detection (ghostty-class default)** (XL, design)
  Target ghostty/kitty/wezterm as tier 1 (kitty keyboard protocol, kitty graphics or sixel, synchronized output DEC 2026, high fps), xterm-class as tier 2 (escape-timeout keys, cell grid, batching and diff rendering), and line mode as tier 3. Detection is in-band (XTGETTCAP, `CSI ? u`, DECRQM), so it works the same over SSH and iroh.
  - Status: not started. `grep -rn -i 'kitty\|XTGETTCAP\|DECRQM\|2026h\|sixel' pkgs/id/src pkgs/id/examples` finds nothing; key parsing is legacy-byte heuristics in pkgs/id/examples/roc-world/Key.roc.
  - Source: RPT §14 (all); RPT §16 Q6
  - Prerequisites: #545 — D1-042 Alternate screen for the raw interactive SSH session, #561 — D1-043 Server-side redraw batching (few-ms frame coalescing) for all presentations, #562 — D1-044 Incremental (diff) ANSI renderer instead of full clear-repaint
- [ ] **D1-053 — Kitty keyboard protocol on the raw input path** (M, design)
  Negotiate the kitty keyboard protocol (`CSI > u`) where supported, so Escape vs Alt is unambiguous and key events go beyond the legacy byte stream; extend `Key.parse` and the browser encoder to match.
  - Status: not started. Key.parse decodes legacy sequences only (pkgs/id/examples/roc-world/Key.roc; RPT §2 lists the tag union). No negotiation in world_ssh.rs.
  - Source: RPT §14 Tier 1 and last paragraph
  - Prerequisites: D1-052 Presentation capability tiers with in-band terminal detection (ghostty-class default) (in this list)

## Source

- REF:106-112, 135-149 (shape 3, triggers)
- REF:161-164
- REF:88-93 (shape 1)
- RPT §12 Later
- RPT §14 (all)
- RPT §14 Tier 1 and last paragraph
- RPT §16 Q3

Both are uncommitted reports in the `platform-world-apps-migration` worktree.

issue.title: id: Phase 13 first slice — shell contract (F13.1), SSH transports (F13.2/F13.3), F13.7 design
issue.body:
## Summary

Phase 13 first slice: F13.1 shell contract, F13.2 SSH frame transport, F13.3 SSH-over-iroh, and the F13.7 design (implementation gated). No new frame kinds are added anywhere in this PR.

```text
shell (terminal / web / native)
  │  ClientFrame / ServerFrame JSON (shell contract v1, pkgs/id/contract/)
  ├─ iroh QUIC stream      /id-world/1        (existing)
  ├─ SSH exec channel      id-world/1         (F13.2, new)
  └─ WebSocket             /ws/world          (existing)
third-party ssh ──► id world ssh-tunnel ──► /id-ssh-tunnel/1 ──► host SSH server (F13.3, new)
```

- **F13.1 (#783)** — `pkgs/id/contract/shell-contract.v1.json` is the versioned contract (frames, fields, bounds, classes incl. journaled-vs-ephemeral, session phases, transports, seed-projection rule). Rust validator (`shell_contract.rs`) + `id world contract [--check FILE]`; drift tests pin it to the serde enums/constants; session conformance tests re-assert the F11.11 seed-leak rule; TS port + vitest prove the browser shell passes unchanged; SSH/CLI terminal shells checked too. Spec: `doc/2026-10-25T05-54-40Z_reference_shell_contract/`.
- **F13.2 (#784)** — `id world join --via ssh [user@]host[:port]` over an SSH exec channel, byte-identical frames to the iroh path (lockstep equality test on one world). Host key pinned by fingerprint/`known_hosts` (no TOFU); SSH login grants nothing.
- **F13.3 (#785, partial)** — `/id-ssh-tunnel/1` forwards raw SSH over iroh to the host's loopback SSH server; `id world ssh-tunnel` (listener or `--stdio` ProxyCommand). Verified with the unmodified system OpenSSH client. Remaining: iroh-over-SSH fallback when UDP is denied (needs a non-QUIC transport that does not exist yet) — #785 stays open for that.
- **F13.7 (#789, design only)** — `doc/2026-10-25T05-37-57Z_design_client_capability_providers/`: two-key grant rule, F12.4-manifest shape with `side: client`, audit/replay design, first provider (`client.file.read`). Implementation gated on F12.4 + F12.6 (and F11.12 for its frame kinds). #789 stays open.

> **Gate (F11.12):** journal-format management has NOT landed (only the `JOURNAL_VERSION` refusal exists; see comment on #227). Per the plan, this PR therefore adds **no new frame kind**. Presentation tiers/focus/kitty/client-provider frames stay `reserved` in the contract.

> **Gates not started:** #786/#787 implementation (gated on F11.9 baseline, #542, still open) and #788/#790 implementation — not touched, per brief.

Bugs found by the new conformance check and fixed here: #836 (terminal shells sent frames the host refused). Also filed from the F13.7 design pass: #837–#841.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `id world join --command-mode` `/stats` etc. → host reply `invalid world frame`; SSH `cmd:` `/stats` → `already joined`; contract did not exist.
  **After:** the same sessions pass `id world contract --check` with 0 violations; `/stats` returns `module_info`.
- Tests run locally (rustup 1.99.0 toolchain, `cargo test --features ssh`):
  - `--lib` filtered suites (shell_contract, contract_tests, world_ssh, frames, world_net, commands::world/serve): 64+ passed, 0 failed; lockstep iroh-vs-SSH equality test stable across 6 runs.
  - `--test cli_integration`: `test_world_contract_*`, `test_world_join_via_ssh_carries_the_frame_protocol`, `test_world_ssh_tunnel_carries_join_via_ssh` pass.
  - Web: `bun run test` (389 passed incl. 15 new contract tests), `bun run typecheck`, biome clean.
  - Manual: system OpenSSH client through `id world ssh-tunnel` played roc-counter (`count=0` → `/input` → `count=1`, `/stats` ok).
- `cargo fmt --check` on touched files: clean. Clippy (`--all-targets --features ssh`): no new warnings in touched files (pre-existing crate warnings remain).
- Not run: full `cargo test --all-features` suite and `nix flake check` locally (time); PR CI re-runs them (previous run's nix check was cancelled at ~60m as infra timeout, not a code failure).

Closes #783, #784. Refs #785, #789, #227, #836, #837, #838, #839, #840, #841.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** contained

Additive transports and a new contract file; no frame kinds, no journal changes, no guest ABI changes. The one host behavior change: joined sessions now answer `info` (authorized by the session's own capability, like `records`), and SSH exec `id-world/1` is accepted where exec was previously always refused. SSH servers stay opt-in via `--world-ssh-port`.

issue.body:
## What and why

Clients connect to several worlds and servers and to other clients at once, and `id` is often client and server simultaneously. A client-only mode must always exist (cheap web load, SSH-only clients); SSH servers in `id` stay rare and opt-in.

## Source

- [Phase 13 plan](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/.opencode/plans/phase-13-client-shells.md) — F13.8
- #564 (Phase 13 plan task)
- #536 (transport designs) — D1-056

## Current status

Partial. `id world join/stats/logs/record/replay` already act as remote iroh clients (pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs WorldClient), and one serve process hosts many worlds (pkgs/id/src/world_hub.rs). Simultaneous multi-world client sessions and a documented client-only mode were not found.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One client holds live sessions to two worlds at once
- [ ] The client-only flag boundary is documented and tested to add no authority (a client never silently becomes a server)
- [ ] A world's journal is unchanged by a second client joining it

## Size

L

## Prerequisites

- #564 (Phase 13 plan task) — F13.1 shell contract

issue.body:
## What and why

Extend scopes, roles and ceilings to named, granted, ceilinged capability providers that run on the client for local resources (a bounded local file read, a GPU buffer, a native notification), keeping the Phase 12 rule that no authority path exists outside named ceilinged providers. The guest requests them through the existing capability protocol; the reply is a bounded capability reply, never a new host-authority path.

## Source

- [Phase 13 plan](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/.opencode/plans/phase-13-client-shells.md) — F13.7
- #564 (Phase 13 plan task)
- #538 (native client shells and client capabilities) — D1-055

## Current status

Not started. Capability execution is host-side only (pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs); the catalog is hard-coded (the `CATALOG` constant in pkgs/id/src/world_caps.rs).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A client provider is added without editing the host `CATALOG` (F12.4 manifest shape)
- [ ] It appears under a ceiling, is refused when over it, and leaves an audit entry (F12.6 contract)
- [ ] It adds no Wasm import (the guest stays import-free, pkgs/id/src/sandbox.rs:1-8)
- [ ] The design answers "who grants" (world/admin vs the client's own user)

## Size

XL

## Prerequisites

- #534 (tracking) — D1-022 F12.4 capability provider registry (manifested components)
- #534 (tracking) — D1-024 F12.6 structured audit log with OpenTelemetry export

issue.body:
## What and why

Give third-party SSH clients reachability to NAT'd `id` hosts by tunnelling SSH over iroh (tailnet-like); iroh-over-SSH only where UDP is blocked but port 22 is open. SSH servers in `id` stay rare and opt-in.

## Source

- [Phase 13 plan](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/.opencode/plans/phase-13-client-shells.md) — F13.3
- #564 (Phase 13 plan task)
- #536 (transport designs) — D1-051

## Current status

Not started. `grep -rn 'tunnel\|direct_tcpip' pkgs/id/src/world_ssh.rs` finds no tunnel or port-forward code; the relay kit's tunnel.toml is an iroh-relay deploy config, not this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An unmodified `ssh` client connects to a world behind NAT through the tunnel
- [ ] A test proves the iroh-over-SSH fallback negotiates when UDP is denied
- [ ] Trust stays at host keys + peer IDs: a peer that reaches the SSH server through iroh still authenticates to `id` normally (no identity bypass)

## Size

L

## Prerequisites

- #564 (Phase 13 plan task) — F13.2 SSH transport (built on top)
